distractors.reason: 'Fast' describes speed of movement, like a fast car. We don't usually say 'fast shower' for a short wash; the natural phrase is 'quick shower'.
'Big' describes size. A shower is not described as 'big' to mean short or brief, so this phrase does not fit the routine.
'High' is used for height or levels, like 'high temperature'. We don't say 'high shower' for a short wash.

example_sentence: Every morning I take a ___ shower before work.
l1_interference: Falantes de português costumam dizer 'fast shower' porque 'rápido' se traduz como 'fast' em muitos contextos. Em inglês, para um banho curto, usamos 'quick'.
explanation: In English, 'quick' is the natural adjective for short actions in daily routines, such as a quick shower, a quick breakfast or a quick look at the news.

related_collocations.example: I love a hot shower on cold mornings.
I need a cup of strong coffee to wake up.
There was heavy traffic on my way to work.

memory_tip: QUICK = short and fast, used for routines (quick shower, quick breakfast) | FAST = speed of movement (fast car, fast runner)
